label: Late original-phase input that is not from the set {x,3,m,l,h,b,z,v,e,y}, after at least two tokens from that set have been seen
explanation: Active almost only in the original (input) phase. 99.9% of activation mass falls there, and it is silent at t<2, in the copy phase, and nearly silent on <DEL>. The firing rate rises with position (orig_idx 3 gives 7%, orig_idx 7-8 gives 34%) and is highest on the last 1-3 inputs before <DEL>. Within that window it depends on history: it fires when the earlier inputs include tokens from a set H={x,3,m,l,h,b,z,v,e,y} (these dominate first_tok and prev2_tok lift) and the current input is NOT in H. Current inputs u, 2, 0, o, c, f, n and d give the highest rates, and u produces the top activations. It is weaker on repeated tokens (in_first=0 has 0.3x lift). The neuron behaves like a graded linear accumulator over the token history, not a crisp rule. Dev F1 is about 0.61 with mass recall about 0.90. False positives are mostly sequences that open with tokens like i, j, o, n, which appear to suppress it. A plain signed-count version of this suppression scored worse.
